Hi Sarah / Marcus —

Excited to kick off the hands-on POC with Acme Financial. To make the sessions useful for both product and ops teams, we want to run a short kickoff followed by two hands-on deep dives focused on:
- prompt & prompt templates review
- routing and fallback policies (smart routing rules)
- a brief load test to validate throughput/latency at expected concurrency

Because your team spans multiple regions, we'd like to propose a rotating schedule so different stakeholders can join a convenient window each week. Can you confirm availability for the options below (times listed in your local time if possible, but I included PT equivalents):

Option A (prefer start-of-day for US): Tue Jun 29, 10:00–12:00 PT (0700–0900 ET / 1500–1700 CET) — Kickoff + hands-on session 1
Option B (late-evening for EU / early-APAC friendly): Thu Jul 1, 21:00–23:00 PT (0000–0200 ET / 0800–1000 SGT next day) — Hands-on session 2 + load test

If neither fits, tell us two 2-hour windows in the next two weeks and we'll rotate accordingly. I attached a rough kickoff agenda (kickoff-agenda-v1.pdf) and a one-row ask: please include the names/roles of your attendees and the person who will approve a short non-prod key for load tests.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning calendars.

Best,
Kimberly Park

+1 on the plan. A few technical constraints to note for the load test and hands-on so Acme's infra doesn't get surprised:

- Load test scope: 1 hour, expected peak throughput target = 200 QPS (50 concurrent users with batching).
- Use non-prod API keys and a separate model variant (quantized) to avoid tax on production capacity.
- We'll flush KV caches before the load and enable continuous batching to simulate typical production traffic.
- If you want deterministic latency numbers, we should reserve a dedicated pool (4x A100 equivalent) for that 1-hour window; otherwise results will be noisy.
- I'll need Marcus or Sarah to confirm the approver email for the non-prod key and whether their tests will hit our endpoints from within an allowlisted IP range.

Attached is a short load-test playbook (load-test-plan.md) with the commands we'll run and the metrics we'll capture. If all good, I'll provision the pool and post the invite with the test steps.

Diego
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
